newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW - Year-end rush seen in Hong Kong IPO market.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Year-end rush seen in Hong Kong IPO market.

text.p: A year-end rush of initial public offerings (IPOs) is expected to hit the Hong Kong stock market, with issuers hoping to take advantage of recent strength in prices and a market acceptance of new issues, analysts said.
"The current market strength and liquidity are favourbale for smaller IPOs," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment.
Analysts said there was some uncertainty about market direction next year, despite overall bullish sentiment, pushing companies to list sooner rather than later.
"It is understandable that many companies are trying to take advantage of the market strength and have their companies listed before the year-end," said one analyst.
"Uncertainty over any possible change in listing rules after the 1997 handover also contributes to the rush." Hong Kong will return to Chinese rule on midnight of June 30, 1997.
Analysts said listing candidates may also be rushing to list ahead of the year-end to match IPOs with their fiscal year.

"A rush to match their fiscal year-end date is expected to boost the number of IPOs," said Wilson Pong, associate director from Nikko Securities. "If there is a delay, it may take months for them to re-prepare listing documents."

Analysts said if candidates cannot list within the current financial year, they may need to revise all the accounting documents prepared for the listing. Preparation of the documents normally takes a few months to complete.
Among upcoming IPOs, computer casing maker Karrie International Holdings Ltd and leather concern Guangdong Tannery Ltd are due to debut on Monday.
Karrie offered 90 million new shares at HK$1.15 each in an IPO which was 60.7 times subscribed.

Guangdong Tannery, a unit of Guangdong Investment Ltd, registered the highest subscription level for its Hong Kong IPO this year. It offered 110 million new shares, of which 30 million shares were offered for public subscription. The public portion was 667 times subscribed.

Satellite services provider APT Satellite Holdings Ltd launched a 10.5 million share offering in Hong Kong last week at HK$17.71 per share, as part of a global offering of 105 million shares. Trading in its stock is due to begin on December 18.

Electrical cable maker Perennial International Ltd is offering 60 million shares at HK$1.07 per share. Public subscription began on Friday and will run until December 18, with dealing in the shares due to begin on December 30.

Electronics concern K&P International Holdings Ltd also launched a 55 million share IPO last week at HK$1.00 each. The offering will close on December 17 and trading in the shares is due to begin on January 2.

Shandong Xinhua Pharmaceutical Co Ltd is expected to run a public offering for new H-shares from December 17 to 20, with trading in the shares expected to start on December 31 and plywood manufacturer Tai Fu International Holdings Ltd and artificial Christmas tree maker FT Holdings Ltd are also expected to launch IPOs soon, analysts said.
"These small IPOs are mainly targeting retail investors who are looking for short-term profit," said Sunny Chan, research manager at Seapower Research.
